To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we show that recurrent neural networks are able to learn a useful embedding of a new word from just one example sentence, (ii) the learned representation is able to generalize to other unseen sentences, and (iii) we demonstrate that the learned representation is interpretable, and that the network learns to exploit its prior knowledge to infer the meaning of a new word.
We show that a deep recurrent neural network can learn a useful representation of a word by observing just one or a few examples of its use.

we can train a deep recurrent network to do one-shot learning of word embedding by using an additional input that encodes the syntactic context of a word, and that the resulting word embedding is useful for downstream NLP tasks such as word analogy and sentiment classification.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we can learn useful representations of words from a single example by using a recurrent neural network to learn a representation of the context in which a word appears, and then learning a representation of the word that is aligned with the learned context.
the recurrent neural network architecture is very flexible, and can be adapted to a wide range of tasks, including one-shot or few shot learning, by simply modifying the objective function.
